title: Strategic Purchasing Decision Framework
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview

Purpose: This framework defines how Redwood evaluates, approves, and processes significant purchasing decisions that materially affect cash, committed capacity (e.g., Dedicated contracts), or revenue recognition. The goal is to balance speed with financial control, legal risk mitigation, and forecasting accuracy.

Scope: Applies to all purchase requests and contract commitments originating from Redwood teams where any of the following apply: total committed value >= $50,000, multi-year commitments, capacity reservations (Dedicated), or purchases that introduce new vendor-hosted data flows.

Principles

- Treat strategic purchases as cross-functional decisions: Procurement, Finance, Legal, Product/Engineering, and GTM should be involved where appropriate.
- Prioritize forecast alignment: commit decisions must map to the rolling forecast within 48 hours of approval.
- Surface revrec impact early: any purchase with billing implications for customers or that changes revenue timing must be escalated to RevRec owners.
- Reduce procurement cycle time while retaining controls: default SLAs for standard requests are 5 BD; strategic requests are 15 BD.

Decision Categories and Triggers

1) Operational Purchase: 
- Definition: Day-to-day purchases, software subscriptions, third-party SaaS under $50k annualized.
- Approval: Manager + Procurement.
- Forecasting impact: Nominal; add to next month’s operating forecast.

2) Strategic Purchase: 
- Definition: Any purchase >= $50k (one-time or annualized), multi-year commitments, Dedicated/Reserved capacity, or vendor requiring data residency/KMS arrangements.
- Approval: Finance Director + Procurement Lead + Legal Review + Product/Eng stakeholder signoff. For purchases >= $250k, include VP Finance signoff.
- Forecasting impact: Must be added to quarter forecast, and FP&A must create a committed line item.

3) Capitalizable Purchase (CapEx candidate): 
- Definition: Hardware, on-prem packages, or purchases that meet capitalization thresholds per accounting policy.
- Approval: Finance Controller + Procurement + Engineering owner + Capital Committee (if > $250k).
- RevRec/Billing: Coordinate with RevRec owner for capitalization and depreciation schedule.

Approval Matrix (summary)

Threshold | Typical Approvers | Procurement Action | Finance Action
---------|------------------|-------------------|----------------
<$50k    | Manager, Procurement | PO creation, standard vendor terms | Expense to ops forecast
$50k-$250k | Finance Director, Procurement, Legal | Contract review, negotiate term limits, SLA requirements | Add to committed forecast; update cash plan
>$250k   | VP Finance + Finance Controller + Legal + Procurement + Exec sponsor | Exec-level negotiation, CFO notification, Treasury hold if prepayment > 30 days | Capital committee review (if capitalizable); update long-range forecast

Step-by-step Strategic Purchase Process

1) Intake (Requester)
- Create procurement request in the Procurement portal with the following fields: business justification, budget code, requested vendor, term, expected start date, expected annualized spend, classification (Operational/Strategic/Capital), and product owner.
- Attach vendor questionnaire (security and data flow) when vendor will handle customer data.

2) Initial Triage (Procurement / Tech Sourcing) - SLA: 2 BD
- Confirm classification and required reviewers per matrix.
- Run vendor risk scan (third-party risk score, public infra dependencies).
- If vendor will host customer data or requires KMS access, mark as High Risk and trigger Legal and Security review.

3) Finance & Forecasting Alignment - SLA: 3 BD
- FP&A assesses cash impact and where to place the committed spend in the forecast (quarter and month).
- For Dedicated/reserved capacity: identify whether this commits Redwood to a pass-through billing model or changes customer pricing. Notify RevRec owner.

4) Legal Review - SLA: 5-10 BD depending on complexity
- Execute standardized commercial terms where possible. Required clauses to check: data residency, KMS/HSM access, audit rights, SLA (uptime target and credit formula), indemnity limits, PI/PHI handling.
- Use the contract clause library: require redwood-standard KMS clause v2.1 for any vendor with access to encryption keys.

5) Negotiation & PO Issuance
- Procurement negotiates pricing, term length, auto-renewal caps, and termination rights.
- Create PO and route to Finance for commitment accounting. For prepayments > 30 days or > $250k total, create a Treasury notice.

6) Onboarding and Invoice Routing
- Vendor onboarding team executes technical onboarding (integration, monitoring endpoints, SLAs). Finance sets invoice routing: invoices@redwood.com with PO reference.
- For recurring billing, set up schedule in Billing system. For Dedicated capacity, coordinate with Product Billing to create customer-visible SKU if pass-through.

RevRec and Forecasting Rules (practical guidance)

- Committed multi-year purchases: record committed liability in the rolling forecast and annotate the RevRec owner. If the spending creates customer billable capacity (e.g., reserved nodes sold to customers), RevRec must model deferred revenue and go-live triggers.
- Prepayments and deposits: treat as prepaid expense until the service is delivered. Add a RevRec trigger checklist item in the contract metadata.
- Cutover to Billing: when a vendor contract creates a new customer-facing SKU or materially changes unit economics, notify Pricing & Billing team at least 10 BD before activation.

Required Contract Clauses (quick reference)

- Data residency: explicit region commitments and breach notification timelines (<= 48 hours).
- Key management (KMS/HSM): explicit statements on whether vendor has access to plaintext keys, key rotation window, and export controls.
- SLA: uptime target (example 99.9% monthly); credits formula and measurement window.
- Audit and SOC evidence: annual SOC2 Type II or equivalent; for high-risk vendors require penetration test results within 12 months.
- Termination: 90-day termination for convenience for strategic commitments where possible; if not, require buyout formula.

PO Example (sample JSON payload to attach to procurement request)

{
  "vendor": "AcmeML Ops",
  "description": "Reserved inference capacity (20 GPUs), 12-month term",
  "annualized_value": "$312000",
  "start_date": "2026-03-01",
  "account_code": "ENG-INF-DED",
  "requested_by": "alice.taylor@redwood.com"
}

Escalations and Exception Handling

- If Legal cannot approve within SLA due to novel terms, the legal reviewer should escalate to Legal Lead and Procurement Lead within 3 BD.
- For emergency purchases (security incident remediation), Procurement may approve with retroactive executive notification; document the incident ID and attach the post-hoc procurement review to the request.

Operational Metrics and Reporting

- Cycle time (intake to PO): target <= 10 BD for strategic, <= 5 BD for operational.
- % of strategic contracts reviewed by Legal: target 100%.
- Forecast accuracy delta attributable to commitments: target < 2% monthly variance.
- Percentage of vendor contracts with required security clauses present at signature: target 98%.

Roles and Responsibilities

- Requester (Product/Engineering/Team Lead): Provide business justification, budget owner, and required technical attachments.
- Procurement: Triage, vendor negotiation, PO creation, vendor onboarding liaison.
- Finance (FP&A / Controller): Forecast placement, commitment accounting, RevRec coordination.
- Legal: Contract review, clause negotiation, risk acceptance.
- Security: Vendor security assessment and recommended controls.

Appendix A — Sample Onboarding Checklist (owner: Procurement)

- Contract signed and stored in contract repository (Confluence link).
- PO created and finance commitment recorded.
- Vendor security questionnaire completed and reviewed.
- KMS/HSM access scoping completed (if applicable).
- Invoice routing and payment terms recorded.
- Technical onboarding meeting scheduled and noted in calendar.

Appendix B — Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Who decides if a purchase is "strategic"?
A: Procurement makes the initial classification during triage; Finance and Legal review and can reclassify during approval flow.

Q: How do Dedicated capacity commitments get represented in the forecast?
A: FP&A creates a committed line item, tags it to the product owner and RevRec owner, and models cash outflows and potential revenue pass-through in the quarter the capacity becomes billable.

Q: What if a vendor refuses our standard KMS clause?
A: Legal will attempt to negotiate acceptable mitigations (segregated keys, key-access logging, additional audit rights). If risk remains, Legal issues a risk acceptance memo and escalates to VP Finance for approval.
